papers.title: Towards a Modular Testing Environment for Digital Battery Passports
papers.venue: Procedia Computer Science
papers.key_contribution: Argues for a freely accessible test platform in which battery distributors and other parties can check their data, interfaces, and system functions against regulatory and technical requirements. It lists the functions, process models, and test types that such a platform needs, including emulation of central components.
papers.classification_scheme: The abstract names three validation targets (data structures, interaction protocols, security mechanisms) and two platform features (modular test procedures, emulation of central components). Finer class lists are not in the abstract; the full text could not be read (the publisher page returned HTTP 403).
papers.conformance_relevance: Closest published statement of the engine's own purpose for the battery case. Existing checks by target: data structures -> data.jsonschema, data.context, data.rules, aas.validate; interaction protocols -> identifier.resolve, api.contract, registry.consistency (mock registry only); security mechanisms -> access.restricted_fields, integrity.jws. Emulated central components exist today only as registry.mock; registry.official stays interface_only. New capability: a catalogue of modular test procedures per role (for example distributor or service provider) and emulators for further central components. The 2027 start date is the paper's statement (secondary_only); the legal source is Regulation (EU) 2023/1542, to be cited from the prior record batteries-regulation.json.
papers.notes: Also in l01 (service-class reference architecture). Crossref: title, first author, year, and journal match.

papers.title: Explainability-Oriented Semantic Validation for Digital Product Passports in Industrial Systems
papers.venue: 2026 1st International Conference on Human Centric Artificial Intelligence (ICHCAI)

An explanation model turns SHACL findings into four parts: violation, interpretation, operational impact, recommended action. A small SHACL prototype and two public CIRPASS datasets show that identifier declaration, access-control specification, storage strategy, interoperability, and security are covered unevenly across current initiatives.
papers.classification_scheme: Five requirement areas named in the abstract: identifier declaration, access-control specification, storage strategy, interoperability, security. Validation dimensions were derived from a CIRPASS standards dataset. Explanation model with four fields.
papers.conformance_relevance: Supports the acceptance route for data.shacl (interface_only): pinned local shapes whose results are compared with the JSON Schema path. The four-field explanation model suggests a static table from reason codes to guidance in the report layer, with no language model at run time (repository rule 4); the abstract does not say that a language model is used. The five uneven requirement areas are a candidate list of ICS fields. Existing checks: data.jsonschema and data.rules overlap with shape constraints; no registered check expresses graph shapes. New capability: data.shacl with pySHACL (prior id pypi-pyshacl) and a reason-code explanation table.
papers.notes: Also in l01. Crossref gives the full author name used here.

Registration and confidentiality can be probed in part: registry.consistency (mock registry only) and access.restricted_fields. The engine must not describe any result as legal compliance (repository documentation rule). Existing checks: manual.review, registry.consistency, access.restricted_fields. papers.title: Digital Product Passports: A Systematic Literature Review on Framework Design and Validation
papers.venue: Digital
papers.key_contribution: Systematic review of peer-reviewed DPP frameworks that rates both design elaboration and validation maturity. Most studies are conceptual or architectural. Validation is mostly an illustrative case study, a stakeholder assessment, or a prototype. Few studies test scalability, interoperability, or operation over the whole lifecycle.
papers.classification_scheme: Two axes. (1) Framework archetype: data-centric, layered, technology-anchored, ecosystem-oriented. (2) Validation maturity: illustrative case study, stakeholder-informed assessment, prototype; explicit empirical validation is rare. Definitions inside each class were not read.
papers.conformance_relevance: Evidence for the gap that a black-box engine fills: cross-organisational testing and interoperability evaluation are named as missing. The validation-maturity axis can give vocabulary for claim levels in conformance test reports (the architecture contract defines claim levels in its section 4; its content was not re-read for this file). A recorded black-box run is a stronger class of evidence than a case study, but still not a legal compliance statement. Existing checks: none apply to the review itself. New capability: none; reuse the maturity vocabulary in method documentation.

papers.title: REECO DIGITAL PRODUCT PASSPORT Conformance Report
papers.venue: Zenodo (preprint, CC-BY-4.0); deposited 2026-08-06
papers.key_contribution: Full text read. A single-author report on conformance tests of passports from one issuer, run on one day (2026-06-11) in four sessions: validation with the CIRPASS-2 reference validator and mock registry, an issuer fix with re-issue, a JSON-LD extension context, and a run of the UN/CEFACT three-tier test suite. It reports three issuer defects found, fixed, and re-tested the same day (a schema violation, a signed form that content negotiation did not reach, and vocabulary terms that the JSON-LD context did not define), one design decision, and three defects in the test tools themselves.
papers.classification_scheme: Layers checked on one passport: official JSON Schema (pinned by a SHA-256 digest); W3C credential schema; JSON-LD expansion in safe mode (terms the context does not define are dropped, which fails the test); RDF validity; signature on the signed form; registry registration with a signed proof. Test-suite tiers: 1 (credential schema and JSON-LD), 2 (schema), 3 (RDF and trust chain). Every finding is labelled issuer defect or instrument defect; a layer that could not be exercised is reported as not assessable.
papers.conformance_relevance: The only concrete DPP conformance report found, and a source of failure modes for the engine. Lessons, in order: (1) Pin the oracles: the report records commit hashes, container image digests, and the schema digest, and keeps log digests in a manifest; every engine report should do the same. (2) Separate issuer defects from instrument defects: the tested validator sent any JSON-LD document that has a context member to its SHACL branch, so a schema check was unreachable for a native passport; the author used a derived copy without the context, and states that this derivation adds one known artefact. The engine should never alter a SUT document silently; any derivation must be a labelled observation. (3) Content negotiation: the first pass wrongly concluded that no signed form existed; it existed but needed an Accept header. identifier.resolve has accept and accepted_media_types parameters that can express this. A check that the signed payload id equals the id of the default representation is not registered as such (integrity.jws compares a payload; identifier.consistency with compare_item compares two JSON documents). (4) JSON-LD expansion: data.context checks only an allowlist and fetches nothing; a check that expands a document with pinned local contexts and fails when terms are dropped is not registered. (5) Report what could not be assessed (the trust-chain tier) as not assessable; this agrees with repository rule 7. (6) The mock registry rejected the passport only when its validation switch was on, and that switch was off by default; registry.consistency must record the validation mode of the mock. (7) A defect class: passports issued before a fix declared a backup URL whose host did not resolve; identifier.resolve on a URL read from registry metadata would detect it. (8) Claim wording: the author refuses terms such as certified or compliant and claims only a pass against pinned schema and reference implementations; this matches the engine's wording rule. Existing checks: data.jsonschema, data.context, integrity.jws, identifier.resolve, identifier.consistency, registry.consistency. New capability: JSON-LD expansion check with pinned local contexts; evidence.untp_dcc (interface_only); a way to import results of an external three-tier suite as signed manual results.
papers.notes: DOI ...739 is the Zenodo concept DOI (OpenAlex and DataCite); the record and version DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.21825740. Self-published by the issuer's founder; all findings are the author's own claims and were not re-checked; no live system was contacted. The report also quotes clause numbers of several EN documents and describes their content in a back-up service section; those statements are not recorded here (repository rule 5). A related GitHub repository named in the record was not opened.

papers.title: Enhancing Digital Product Passports with Material Fingerprinting and Decentralized Non-Conformity Signals: Application to Critical Raw Materials
papers.venue: Procedia Computer Science
papers.key_contribution: Architecture and data model of the Ma-DiTraCe project built on self-sovereign identity and verifiable credentials. Material fingerprints from chemical, isotopic, or spectral analysis are signed as credentials to tie the physical material to the digital passport, and a decentralised red-flag mechanism aggregates non-conformity signals for certification management. Blockchain anchoring is optional.
papers.conformance_relevance: Names a physical-to-digital binding failure that digital checks miss: a substituted or non-conforming material still passes metadata checks. identifier.consistency states that digital consistency does not prove physical authenticity; fingerprint evidence is laboratory evidence that only manual.review (signed manual results) or a later credential verifier can carry. A dynamic non-conformity feed is a status problem; integrity.status_list (interface_only) is the nearest hook. Existing checks: integrity.jws, manual.review, identifier.consistency. New capability: integrity.status_list; a verifiable-credential data-model verifier (none registered).
papers.notes: Also in l01 and l02.

papers.title: Zero-Knowledge Proof Extensions for Digital Product Passports in Sustainability Claims Reporting and Verifications

The paper's cost measures (proof verification time per claim) are a workload bound for a future adapter. Existing checks: none. papers.title: Automatic quality assessment of asset administration shell submodel templates
papers.venue: Conference paper in the ZHAW digital collection (the conference name is not stated in the text read)
papers.key_contribution: Full text read. Analyses the 51 official IDTA submodel templates (JSON versions from the IDTA site, merged into one environment, metamodel 3.0 assumed). Eleven of them break the metamodel, and nine groups of recurring issues are found: unexpected cardinality use, arbitrary structures, conflicting re-definitions, dangling references, loose numeric types, unexpected ID-short naming, deprecated elements, inconsistent qualifier kinds, and stray whitespace. A prototype made of independent assessment functions reports warnings and errors with the element path; two engineers built it in five working days, about 3,000 lines of Python on the aas-core library.
papers.classification_scheme: Nine issue groups (listed above) and two severities: warning (usable but inconsistent) and error (blocks automatic processing). The paper's table counts issues per group over the 51 templates; deprecated elements and inconsistent qualifier kinds dominate with more than 2,000 occurrences each. The text and the table of the paper disagree on a few counts (numeric precision, whitespace), so figures are indicative only.
papers.conformance_relevance: Three consequences. (1) Oracle quality: if the engine pins a JSON Schema or rule pack derived from an official template, defects of the template (conflicting definitions, dangling references, deprecated qualifiers) pass into every test; run a template-quality gate when a schema pack is built and record the template version. (2) The paper states that the AAS test tooling covers only two templates (Digital Nameplate and Contact Information) and that no tool checked the template-level constraints written in natural language, so aas.validate gives no assurance for DPP templates. (3) The nine groups are a ready failure-mode list for data.rules on AAS content: dangling references, whitespace in identifiers, deprecated attributes, ambiguous aggregation. The authors plan language-model analysis later; the engine must keep such methods out of run time (repository rule 4). Existing checks: aas.validate, data.jsonschema, data.rules. New capability: a build-time template-quality gate for schema packs; DPP template profiles. The authors name a Zenodo record for their code (not opened).

conformance_implications.implication: Conformance test environments split into data instance validation, isolated systems testing, and peer-to-peer testing. The engine covers the first two; peer-to-peer (interoperability between two implementations) is not covered, and reports must say that interoperability was not tested. Interoperability claims should also name the layer tested.
conformance_implications.existing_check: All registered checks are conformance-type and black-box.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Peer mode with a second implementation (reference implementation or two SUTs), a claim level for interoperability evidence, and a report field for the layer tested.

conformance_implications.implication: Content-level conformance has four test types. Scenario-based multi-step flows have no check.
conformance_implications.existing_check: data.jsonschema; data.rules; aas.validate; identifier.consistency; registry.consistency; persistence.versions
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Scenario runner with ordered steps and shared state (the planner behaviour for step ordering was not checked).

conformance_implications.implication: AAS testing has three layers: metamodel and structure, submodel-template conformity, and API behaviour. aas.validate covers structure and API shape via the wrapped tool. The wrapped tool covers two templates only (confirmed by a 2026 paper, the live PyPI description, and the repository state read on 2026-10-19), so DPP template conformity needs pinned schemas or an upstream contribution. Official templates themselves contain defects, so they are not a clean oracle.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: DPP template profiles (IDTA 02099, 02035-x) as pinned schemas; a template-quality gate at schema-pack build time; behaviour checks on a loopback AAS server.

conformance_implications.implication: Event-triggered re-validation after each update is shown for submodels. In the engine, only version comparison (experimental) exists; scheduled acquisition is interface_only; an MQTT listener is outside the passive pull model.

A DPP test platform needs modular procedures and emulated central components; the engine has a mock registry only. The CIRPASS-2 mock registry and validator are example, non-normative tools, and in a real use the validator's routing of JSON-LD documents blocked a schema check.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: registry.official (interface_only, needs separate authorisation); further emulators; record the validation mode of the mock in each report.

conformance_implications.implication: Semantic validation with SHACL is proposed with an explanation layer and for AAS data entry. The data.shacl acceptance criterion (agreement with the JSON Schema path) is not yet met. Explanations must come from a static reason-code table, not a language model at run time.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: data.shacl with pySHACL and pinned local shapes; explanation table in the report layer.

conformance_implications.implication: Data quality tools in the literature are per-metric value validators (rules) and ML-based validators. Only the deterministic kind can give a verdict. Traceability maturity scores are integer, but measure properties that a black-box run cannot observe.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Sector rule packs as pinned files; optional ICS declaration of maturity; manual.review for the unobservable part.

conformance_implications.implication: Interoperability of credential-based systems depends on several components, and composition of conforming specifications can still be insecure. Real pilots fail on onboarding, wallet and schema compliance, and identity-system interoperability. The engine verifies a JWS only.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Credential data-model verifier, status list (integrity.status_list, interface_only), wallet emulator on loopback. Network resolution of identifiers is excluded from tests.

conformance_implications.implication: Dataspace connectors differ in architecture, data model, and usage-control language. No registered check covers the connector protocol or usage policies.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Connector profile in the ICS; loopback mock connector; policy-language check.

conformance_implications.implication: Identifier services cannot be proven unique or persistent by a finite test; resolver testing literature is thin and does not cover GS1 link resolution. Per-step diagnostics are the useful pattern. A declared backup URL whose host does not resolve is a concrete defect class seen in a real report.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: persistence.scheduled; GS1-conformant resolver profile checks pinned to the GS1 standard (prior id gs1-conformant-resolver-1-2-1), written only from that open standard; resolution of URLs read from registry metadata.

conformance_implications.implication: Specification-derived REST testing is mature (property-based, nominal and error scenarios) and shows that many real APIs deviate from their own OpenAPI description. Fuzzers leave parts of APIs unexercised, so unexercised parts must be reported as not run. api.fuzz is interface_only and needs authorisation and a budget.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: api.fuzz on Schemathesis (prior id pypi-schemathesis) first against a loopback reference system, with recorded seed and requests; fixed negative cases in test packs meanwhile; contract coverage counters.

conformance_implications.implication: Access-control testing has fault models, mutation, and coverage criteria. The engine probes role views per channel; it has no coverage report of the policy matrix and no stateful probes (usage control).
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Policy coverage counters; seeded-leak fixtures for self-tests; stateful probe sequences.

conformance_implications.implication: Integrity evidence in the literature is of three kinds: signed submodels, off-chain data plus on-chain hash, and zero-knowledge proofs. The engine verifies JWS only. Anchors and proofs cannot show that the signed or hashed attributes are true.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Anchor-verification adapter on local fixtures or signed receipts; AAS signature submodel verifier (unsupported today); proof class recorded as unsupported.

conformance_implications.implication: Digital twin verification and validation separates built right from right thing, and own from independent assessment. The engine is an independent verifier of digital consistency and never validates fidelity to the physical product. Laboratory evidence (material fingerprints, measurement traceability) enters only through signed manual results.

DPP literature validates mostly by case study or prototype; cross-organisational testing and interoperability evaluation are named gaps. A conformance test report is a stronger evidence class but is not legal compliance. The one real report found refuses words such as certified and claims only a pass against pinned artefacts.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: evidence.untp_dcc and evidence.qualified_seal (both interface_only) for later trust-service links.

conformance_implications.implication: Carrier failure modes (counterfeit carriers, cloned tags) are named but not tested by any paper in this scope. NFC and RFID checks need a physical tag campaign.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: carrier.nfc and carrier.rfid with a recorded tag campaign (interface_only today).

conformance_implications.implication: The oracle can be wrong. In the REECO report, the validator, the test suite, and a mock registry each had a defect that blocked or falsified a verdict; in Miny 2026, 51 official templates held many defects. The engine must pin every oracle by version and digest, record the pins in each report, keep a defect in the instrument apart from a defect in the SUT, and never alter a SUT document silently.
conformance_implications.existing_check: All checks that use pinned local resources (data.jsonschema, data.context, data.rules, api.contract, aas.validate).
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: Report fields for oracle pins and digests; an outcome that marks a layer as not assessable because of an instrument limit; a template-quality gate at schema-pack build time.

conformance_implications.implication: Signed and unsigned forms of one passport can sit behind content negotiation; a test that does not send the right Accept header concludes wrongly that no signed form exists. The id and payload of the two forms should be compared.
conformance_implications.existing_check: identifier.resolve (accept and accepted_media_types parameters); integrity.jws; identifier.consistency
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: A pairing of the default and signed representations in one test purpose (fetch both, compare ids).

conformance_implications.implication: JSON-LD conformance needs expansion of the document with its contexts. Terms that the contexts do not define are dropped in safe mode and make the document fail. The data.context check only compares context references with an allowlist and fetches nothing.
conformance_implications.new_capability_needed: A JSON-LD expansion check with pinned local context files (no network) that fails on dropped terms; data.shacl for RDF-level shapes.

cross_paper_observations: DPP literature has almost no test methods of its own. Papers that validate a DPP design use case studies, prototypes, or expert assessment; only one paper (Gering) argues for a test environment and only one grey report (REECO) documents actual conformance test sessions. Test methods have to be taken from adjacent fields: AAS testing, REST API testing, access-control testing, and classic conformance and interoperability testing.

The AAS testing cluster (Wollschlaeger, Schoettke, Miny, Nowshin and colleagues) separates three layers: structure, template conformity, and behaviour of the API. The engine's aas.validate sits on the first layer and partly the third; the DPP-specific template layer is a gap, and the official templates have defects of their own (51 templates analysed, 11 break the metamodel).

Oracle quality is a recurring theme in the two documents read in full: the test tools of one real conformance report each had a defect, and the official AAS templates had many. A conformance engine needs oracle pinning, digests, and an outcome for instrument limits, not only SUT verdicts.

Two older classification schemes (Snelick; Kulvatunyou) give a vocabulary for what kind of test an engine performs. Both support separating conformance evidence from interoperability evidence in claim levels, and a recent framework (Siapera) and an interview study (Acharya) point to naming the interoperability characteristic or layer tested.

Papers use the word interoperability for semantic compatibility of data, for identity-system compatibility, and for protocol compatibility. No DPP paper gives a test for any of them. An engine claim should name which sense was tested.

Identifier and resolver testing has very thin literature. Only an LSID tester (2008), a blog post, and one cross-region GS1/Ecode resolution experiment were located; none tests link-type behaviour of GS1-conformant resolvers.

Access-control testing is a mature field (fault models, mutation, coverage) built around XACML policy engines, and no paper applies it to a DPP. Its concepts transfer to the engine's role-field-channel matrix.

Integrity papers in the DPP field evaluate performance of ledger anchoring, not the soundness of verification. A check that recomputes a canonical digest and compares it with an anchor has no published DPP precedent in this scope.
Data-quality work for DPPs (textile cluster) mixes rule-based validation with ML-based validation. Only rule-based validation fits deterministic verdicts.

Spec-derived REST testing shows that many real APIs deviate from their own descriptions, and that fuzzers leave parts unexercised. A contract check will produce failures that need clear attribution between contract and implementation, and a fuzz run needs a coverage statement.

No STRIDE-style or attacker-model-based threat analysis for DPP systems was located in this scope. The nearest are design-space papers that list counterfeiting, interoperability, and data sovereignty as challenges.
